units.text: Use when the goal is to set up Robolectric for a module, choose or fix its configuration, or get the tests running under a JDK or CI environment.

1. Read the module's build files, the test configuration, and the CI configuration. Record the JDK in use and the Robolectric and Compose versions. Run the tests and record the exact command and result.

2. Check where the tests live. You can convert an instrumented test to Robolectric by moving it to the `test` source set and setting up the Robolectric dependencies: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#quick-reference).

quotes.quote: You can convert an instrumented test to Robolectric by moving it to the test source set and setting up the Robolectric dependencies.

units.text: 3. Check the Robolectric dependencies in the module's `build.gradle`/`build.gradle.kts` file, including `isIncludeAndroidResources`: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#robolectric-dependencies).

quotes.quote: Start by adding the following to your module's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file:
android { testOptions { unitTests { isIncludeAndroidResources = true } } } dependencies { testImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2") testImplementation("org.robolectric:robolectric:4.18") }

units.text: 4. Check the Compose test dependencies in the module containing your UI tests: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#compose-ui-test-dependencies).

quotes.quote: First, add the following dependencies to the build.gradle file of the module containing your UI tests

units.text: 5. Check the Android API levels the tests run against. By default, Robolectric runs your code against the `targetSdk` specified in the module's build file or `AndroidManifest.xml` file: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#sdk-level).

quotes.quote: By default, Robolectric will run your code against the targetSdk specified in your module's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts or AndroidManifest.xml file. If you want to test your code under a different SDK, you can specify the desired SDK(s) using the sdk, minSdk and maxSdk config properties:

units.text: 6. Check the JDK against the minimum Java version for those API levels. The minimum is 17 for API 34 and 35, and 21 for API 36 and 37: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#android).

quotes.quote: This table shows the minimum Java version required to run Robolectric tests against a specific version of Android
Android 17 37 21
Android 16 36 21
Android 15 35 17
Android 14 34 17

units.text: 7. Check whether the tests run on Java 17 or higher. When running tests on Java 17 or higher, the JVM requires `--add-opens` flags so that Robolectric can access internal OpenJDK classes and APIs: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#java-17-and-higher).

quotes.quote: When running tests on Java 17 or higher, the JVM requires --add-opens flags so that Robolectric can access internal OpenJDK classes and APIs (java.lang, java.io, jdk.internal.access, etc.). Add the following jvmArgs to your unit test configuration in build.gradle / build.gradle.kts:

units.text: 8. Check where the test runtime gets its jars. Pre-instrumented android-all jars are published on MavenCentral, and they are lazily downloaded during tests runtime using `MavenArtifactFetcher`: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#android-all-downloads).

quotes.quote: These pre-instrumented Android-all jars are published on MavenCentral
They are lazily downloaded and during tests runtime using MavenArtifactFetcher

units.text: 9. Check the CI machine architecture. Robolectric's native runtime includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (`@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`) can run on Linux arm64 environments. No configuration is needed. The legacy SQLite mode (`SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY`) isn't supported on Linux arm64: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#linux-arm64-runners).

quotes.quote: Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon
No configuration is needed
As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

units.text: 10. If resources may not be loading for a library, enable debug logging by setting the system property `robolectric.logging.enabled = true`: [debugging.md](../debugging/debugging.md#debug-logging).

quotes.quote: If you are not sure if resources are being loaded for a particular library
enable debug logging by setting the system property robolectric.logging.enabled = true and run your tests

units.text: - Report each finding with the build or CI file and line, the documented statement it relies on, and the official page that states it.
- List separately anything about the project that no official page covers, and mark it not documented.
- Give the baseline command and result.
- If the request was only for an explanation or plan, stop here.
- Change only the settings the findings call for, and keep each change traceable to its finding.
- Add the Robolectric dependencies and `isIncludeAndroidResources`: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#robolectric-dependencies).

quotes.quote: Start by adding the following to your module's build.gradle/build.gradle.kts file:
android { testOptions { unitTests { isIncludeAndroidResources = true } } } dependencies { testImplementation("junit:junit:4.13.2") testImplementation("org.robolectric:robolectric:4.18") }

units.text: - For Java 17 and higher, add the `--add-opens` flags as `jvmArgs` in the unit test configuration: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#java-17-and-higher).

quotes.quote: When running tests on Java 17 or higher, the JVM requires --add-opens flags so that Robolectric can access internal OpenJDK classes and APIs (java.lang, java.io, jdk.internal.access, etc.). Add the following jvmArgs to your unit test configuration in build.gradle / build.gradle.kts:

android { testOptions { unitTests.all { it.jvmArgs( "--add-opens=java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.io=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.net=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.security=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/java.text=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.base/jdk.internal.access=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=java.desktop/java.awt.font=ALL-UNNAMED", "--add-opens=jdk.compiler/com.sun.tools.javac.api=ALL-UNNAMED", ) } } }

units.text: - To configure one test class or method, use the `@Config` annotation. Annotations on methods take precedence over class-level ones: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#config-annotation).

quotes.quote: To configure Robolectric for a single test class or method, use the @Config annotation on the desired class or method. Annotations applied on methods take precedence over the ones at the class level.

units.text: - To configure all tests in a package or group of packages, create a `robolectric.properties` file in the appropriate package, generally under `src/test/resources`: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#properties-file).

quotes.quote: To configure all Robolectric tests within a package or group of packages, create a file named robolectric.properties in the appropriate package. Generally, this file would be placed within the appropriate package directory under src/test/resources in your project tree. Robolectric will search for properties files up the hierarchy of packages (including the unnamed default package at the top level), with values in deeper packages overriding values in more shallow packages. When test classes or methods have @Config annotations, those override any config from properties files.

units.text: - `sdk` and `minSdk`/`maxSdk` may not be specified in the same `@Config` annotation or file; `minSdk` and `maxSdk` may be specified together: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#sdk-level).

quotes.quote: Note that sdk and minSdk/maxSdk may not be specified in the same @Config annotation or file; however, minSdk and maxSdk may be specified together. If any of them is present, they override any SDK specification from a less-specific configuration location.

units.text: - Some additional options can be configured globally by setting system properties. When using Gradle, you can configure the system properties for unit tests with the `android.testOptions.unitTests.all` block: [configuration.md](../core/configuration.md#system-properties).

quotes.quote: Some additional options can be configured globally by setting these system properties:
When using Gradle, you can configure the System Properties for unit tests with the android.testOptions.unitTests.all block
to override the Maven repository URL and ID to download the runtime dependencies from a repository other than Maven Central:

units.text: - To download the runtime dependencies from a repository other than Maven Central, set `robolectric.dependency.repo.url` and `robolectric.dependency.repo.id`: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#custom-mirror-and-proxy).

quotes.quote: When using Gradle, you can configure the System Properties for unit tests with the android.testOptions.unitTests.all block
to override the Maven repository URL and ID to download the runtime dependencies from a repository other than Maven Central:
robolectric.dependency.repo.url Set the URL of the Maven repository to use for the runtime dependencies. https://repo1.maven.org/maven2

units.text: - To disable runtime fetching of jars, set `robolectric.offline` to true: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#system-properties).

quotes.quote: robolectric.offline Set to true to disable runtime fetching of jars. false

units.text: - To use the AndroidX test runner in Robolectric tests, use `@RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class)`: [test-suite-structure.md](../core/test-suite-structure.md#androidx-test).

quotes.quote: It is now possible to use the AndroidX test runner in Robolectric tests.
import androidx.test.ext.junit.runners.AndroidJUnit4 @RunWith(AndroidJUnit4::class) class SandwichTest

units.text: - Run the test task for the module and compare the result with the baseline. Record the command and output.
- Run the same task in the CI environment and record the result.
- Remove each added setting in turn and confirm that the failure it addressed returns, then restore it.
- Re-read every setting against its reference file or official page, and drop any you cannot tie to one.

- When a result differs between a device and the JVM, note that Android libcore and OpenJDK have different implementations, so you may notice different behaviours: [ci-cd.md](../infrastructure-ci-cd/ci-cd.md#differences-from-a-device).

quotes.quote: Android libcore and OpenJDK have different implementations
Because of that, you may notice different behaviours when running your app on a device or emulator, and running your tests on the JVM with Robolectric.
